The use of `chmod 4755` on `chrome-sandbox` is notable but not inherently malicious; it is a well-known workaround for Chromium's sandboxing model on systems without user namespaces. This is commonly seen in Electron and other Chromium-derived apps distributed on Linux. There are no network operations, dynamic downloads, obfuscated commands, or file manipulations outside the package build environment. All actions are confined to the build and package directories, and no sensitive system files are accessed or modified.

While distributing prebuilt binaries via AUR carries inherent trust assumptions (users must trust the upstream vendor and the maintainer not to distribute tampered binaries), this PKGBUILD itself does not introduce additional malicious behavior. The package follows standard AUR practices for binary repackaging and does not exhibit signs of supply-chain compromise.
</details>
